title: Gestational Diabetes: Antenatal Glucose Management and Delivery Planning

evidenceAudit.scope: Women with gestational diabetes after diagnosis: glucose monitoring and targets, escalation to metformin or insulin, fetal surveillance, timing and mode of birth, glucose control in labour and caesarean, and neonatal glucose checks. Checked against the Saudi MOH Pocket Manual in Obstetrics & Gynaecology (2014) and NICE NG3. Sections: MOH pp. 166–171; NG3 recommendations 1.2.9–1.2.23, 1.3.1–1.3.5, 1.3.33–1.3.40, 1.4.1–1.4.12 and 1.5.1–1.5.11. Medicine-pathway restructure on 2026-10-18: medicines regrouped into branches, steps and give-all vs choose-one options; no dose, source or clinical claim was re-checked.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 14 Oct 2026.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.

Medicine list restructured into a branched decision pathway on 2026-10-18. Doses, routes, adjustments, monitoring, contraindications and sources are unchanged from authoring-standard-2026-10-14-v1-live.
unverifiedSections: The MOH manual is a 2014 document; whether a newer Saudi national guideline replaced it was not checked.
NG3 1.3.1–1.3.40 cover all types of diabetes; only the parts that apply to gestational diabetes are used here, and pre-existing diabetes in pregnancy is not covered by this topic.
Metformin and glyburide doses were reused from the repository's earlier gestational diabetes topic (FDA label) and were not re-opened on 14 Oct 2026; NICE NG3 gives no dose.
Insulin doses are the MOH total-daily-dose figures; NICE NG3 gives none and titration is specialist work.
The MOH manual text on fetal testing starting at 32 weeks and a caesarean threshold of 4,750 g was read once and is not cross-checked with a second source.
SFDA registration and hospital formulary availability were not independently verified.

Medicine pathway: branch entry criteria, preferred options and “use when” conditions were assigned from this topic's own indications and management steps. Confirm each against the cited guideline before clinical use.

pathophysiology.summary: Placental hormones raise insulin resistance in the second and third trimester; if insulin secretion does not keep up, maternal glucose rises and crosses to the fetus, which responds with extra insulin and growth (summarised from NG3 1.2.1 and the MOH overview, p. 166). Good glucose control throughout pregnancy lowers the risk of macrosomia, birth trauma, induction or caesarean, neonatal hypoglycaemia and perinatal death (NG3 1.2.10). Fasting glucose at diagnosis guides treatment: below 7.0 mmol/L a trial of diet and exercise; 7.0 or above immediate insulin, with or without metformin (NG3 1.2.18, 1.2.22). Maternal glucose in labour drives neonatal hypoglycaemia, so labour glucose is kept between 4 and 7 mmol/L and newborn glucose is checked 2 to 4 hours after birth (NG3 1.4.10, 1.5.3).

symptoms: Usually none; glucose is found by monitoring (NG3 1.2.11).
Symptoms of hypoglycaemia on insulin: sweating, tremor, confusion (advise to carry fast-acting glucose, NG3 1.3.14).
Reduced fetal movements or a large-for-dates uterus prompt review (NG3 1.3.34).
physicalSigns: Capillary glucose readings from self-monitoring against targets (NG3 1.3.5).
Fetal growth and amniotic fluid volume on ultrasound, estimated fetal weight (NG3 1.3.34).
Blood pressure and urine protein at every visit as part of routine antenatal care (NG3 1.3.39).
redFlags: Hyperglycaemia or feeling unwell: test urgently for ketones and seek urgent medical advice (NG3 1.3.22–1.3.23).
Suspected diabetic ketoacidosis: immediate admission to level 2 critical care with obstetric care (NG3 1.3.24).
Fasting plasma glucose 7.0 mmol/L or above at diagnosis: start insulin immediately, with or without metformin (NG3 1.2.22).
Capillary glucose below 4 mmol/L on insulin, or hypoglycaemia that needs help: treat at once and review the dose (NG3 1.3.6).
precipitants: Fasting glucose 7.0 mmol/L or above at diagnosis, or macrosomia or hydramnios with fasting 6.0–6.9 mmol/L (NG3 1.2.22–1.2.23).
Non-adherence to diet, exercise and monitoring (NG3 1.2.11, 1.2.14).
Maternal obesity or comorbidity needing anaesthetic assessment in the third trimester (NG3 1.4.8).

differentials.condition: Pre-existing type 2 diabetes first found in pregnancy
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: HbA1c measured at diagnosis to identify possible pre-existing type 2 diabetes; follow type 1 or type 2 pathway if confirmed (NG3 1.3.10).
Ketonaemia with hyperglycaemia or unwell; level 2 critical care (NG3 1.3.23–1.3.24).

differentials.condition: Fetal growth restriction with vascular disease
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Macrovascular disease or nephropathy needs individualised fetal monitoring rather than the routine schedule (NG3 1.3.36).

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Readings above target for 1–2 weeks despite diet and exercise: add metformin, then insulin (NG3 1.2.19–1.2.21).
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Teach self-monitoring at diagnosis; use the same targets as pre-existing diabetes (NG3 1.2.11–1.2.12, 1.3.5).
ruleIn.normalValue: NICE: fasting below 5.3, 1-hour below 7.8, 2-hour below 6.4 mmol/L; MOH: pre-meal below 95, 1-hour below 140, 2-hour below 120 mg/dL

references.title: NICE NG3: Diabetes in pregnancy: management from preconception to the postnatal period

ruleIn.testName: Ultrasound for fetal growth and amniotic fluid volume
ruleIn.modalityTarget: Woman with gestational diabetes from 28 to 36 weeks
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Large fetus or raised fluid volume changes timing of birth and is a reason to consider insulin with fasting 6.0–6.9 mmol/L (NG3 1.2.23, 1.4.7).
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: NICE offers monitoring every 4 weeks from 28 to 36 weeks; MOH describes growth scans at 28, 32 and 36 weeks (NG3 1.3.34; MOH p. 168).
ruleIn.normalValue: Estimated fetal weight within the centile range; normal fluid volume

references.title: NICE NG3: Diabetes in pregnancy: management from preconception to the postnatal period

ruleIn.modalityTarget: Woman newly diagnosed with gestational diabetes
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Raised HbA1c suggests pre-existing diabetes, raising pregnancy risk above 48 mmol/mol (6.5%) (NG3 1.3.9–1.3.10).
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Do not use HbA1c routinely to judge control in the second and third trimesters (NG3 1.3.11).

references.title: NICE NG3: Diabetes in pregnancy: management from preconception to the postnatal period

ruleOut.modalityTarget: Pregnant woman with diabetes who is hyperglycaemic or unwell
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Ketonaemia with hyperglycaemia: admit to level 2 critical care (NG3 1.3.23–1.3.24).
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Test urgently for ketonaemia whenever a pregnant woman with any form of diabetes is hyperglycaemic or unwell (NG3 1.3.23).

references.title: NICE NG3: Diabetes in pregnancy: management from preconception to the postnatal period

ruleOut.modalityTarget: Baby of a woman with diabetes
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Below 2.0 mmol/L on two consecutive readings despite feeding support: tube feeding or intravenous dextrose (NG3 1.5.10).
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Test routinely at 2 to 4 hours after birth with a quality-assured method validated for neonates (NG3 1.5.3, 1.5.8).

references.title: NICE NG3: Diabetes in pregnancy: management from preconception to the postnatal period

clinicalManagement.title: First week after diagnosis
actions: Review at the joint diabetes and antenatal clinic within 1 week (NG3 1.2.9).
Teach self-monitoring, refer to a dietitian and advise regular exercise such as a 30-minute walk after a meal (NG3 1.2.11, 1.2.16–1.2.17; MOH p. 166).
Measure HbA1c to identify possible pre-existing type 2 diabetes (NG3 1.3.10).

clinicalManagement.title: Monitor against targets
actions: Monitor glucose at the frequency in NG3 1.3.2–1.3.3 and agree individual targets (NG3 1.3.4–1.3.5).
Keep joint clinic contact every 1–2 weeks (NG3 1.3.38).
Give information and education at every appointment (NG3 1.3.40).

clinicalManagement.title: Escalate treatment
actions: Fasting below 7.0 mmol/L: diet and exercise trial; if targets are not met in 1–2 weeks offer metformin; add insulin if still not met; insulin if metformin is unsuitable (NG3 1.2.18–1.2.21).
Fasting 7.0 mmol/L or above, or 6.0–6.9 with macrosomia or hydramnios: consider immediate insulin with or without metformin (NG3 1.2.22–1.2.23).
MOH practice: insulin, with glyburide as an alternative (MOH p. 167). Prefer rapid-acting analogues (NG3 1.3.12).
Advise insulin users to carry fast-acting glucose and to keep capillary glucose above 4 mmol/L (NG3 1.3.6, 1.3.14).

clinicalManagement.title: Fetal surveillance
actions: Ultrasound for fetal anomalies including the heart at 20 weeks (NG3 1.3.33).
Growth and fluid volume ultrasound every 4 weeks from 28 to 36 weeks (NG3 1.3.34); MOH describes antenatal testing from 32 weeks (p. 168).
Routine fetal wellbeing tests before 38 weeks are not recommended unless there is a risk of growth restriction (NG3 1.3.35).

clinicalManagement.title: Plan the birth
actions: Discuss timing and mode of birth in the third trimester (NG3 1.4.1).
Gestational diabetes: birth no later than 40 weeks plus 6 days; consider earlier for complications; offer induction or caesarean if not delivered by then (NG3 1.4.4–1.4.5).
MOH: induction at 39 weeks with good control; scheduled caesarean for estimated fetal weight above 4,750 g (MOH p. 168).
Discuss risks and benefits of vaginal birth, induction and caesarean for a macrosomic fetus (NG3 1.4.7).
Offer anaesthetic assessment in the third trimester for obesity or autonomic neuropathy (NG3 1.4.8).

clinicalManagement.title: Labour and birth
actions: Check capillary glucose hourly and keep it between 4 and 7 mmol/L (NG3 1.4.10).
Use intravenous dextrose and insulin if out of range (NG3 1.4.12). MOH: glucose every 2 hours, start insulin infusion above 120 mg/dL, adjust per local protocol (MOH p. 170).
Caesarean: hold the morning dose, give 5% dextrose, check glucose hourly, insulin infusion for raised glucose (MOH p. 169).
General anaesthesia: monitor glucose every 30 minutes until fully conscious (NG3 1.4.9).

clinicalManagement.title: Care of the baby
actions: Keep the baby with the mother unless complications arise (NG3 1.5.2).
Feed within 30 minutes, then every 2–3 hours; test glucose at 2–4 hours (NG3 1.5.3, 1.5.9).
Tube feed or give intravenous dextrose only if glucose below 2.0 mmol/L twice, abnormal signs or ineffective feeding (NG3 1.5.10).
Do not transfer to community care before 24 hours of age with stable glucose and good feeding (NG3 1.5.6).

regimens.indication: Gestational diabetes not at target after 1–2 weeks of diet and exercise (NICE NG3 1.2.19)
regimens.dose: 500 mg twice daily (or 850 mg once daily) with meals
regimens.frequency: Increase by 500 mg weekly per glucose and tolerance
adjustments: Label dose is for type 2 diabetes; use in pregnancy follows NICE NG3
Stop before iodinated contrast if eGFR 30–60
contraindications: Acute or chronic metabolic acidosis including DKA
regimens.sourceTitle: Metformin hydrochloride prescribing information (US FDA label, DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: NICE NG3, Recommendations 1.2.19–1.2.21 (indication); dose from the FDA label as accessed 12 Oct 2026, Section 2

regimens.dose: Total daily dose 0.7 units/kg (1st trimester), 0.8 units/kg (2nd), 0.9 units/kg (3rd)
regimens.duration: Until birth; stop after birth in GDM
adjustments: Titrate to capillary targets; keep glucose above 4 mmol/L
Extra insulin needed with antenatal corticosteroids
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to the insulin or excipients
regimens.sourceTitle: MOH Pocket Manual in Obstetrics & Gynaecology, Saudi Ministry of Health
regimens.sourceEdition: MOH Pocket Manual 2014, p. 167 (insulin therapy); NICE NG3 Recommendations 1.2.20–1.2.22 for when to start; NG3 1.3.12 prefers rapid-acting analogues

regimens.indication: Alternative to insulin for glycaemic control in gestational diabetes (Saudi MOH)
regimens.dose: 2.5–5 mg once daily with breakfast (1.25 mg if at risk of hypoglycaemia)
adjustments: Starting dose from the FDA label (type 2 diabetes); MOH lists glyburide as an alternative to insulin — NICE does not recommend it
regimens.sourceTitle: Glyburide (glibenclamide) tablets prescribing information (US FDA label, DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: MOH Pocket Manual 2014, p. 167 (non-insulin therapy); dose from the FDA label as accessed 12 Oct 2026, Section 2

regimens.indication: Labour or birth with capillary glucose outside 4–7 mmol/L (NICE NG3 1.4.12); MOH: blood sugar above 140 mg/dL in established labour
regimens.dose: 10 units in 1,000 mL dextrose 5% at 100–125 mL/h, or 0.5–1 unit/h with dextrose 5% 100 mL/h
adjustments: Hold insulin if glucose below 140 mg/dL
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to the insulin or excipients

regimens.sourceEdition: MOH Pocket Manual 2014, p. 170 (labour and delivery); NICE NG3 Recommendations 1.4.10–1.4.12

medicationPlan.note: NICE NG3 sets when to add metformin or insulin and the labour glucose range but gives no doses (1.2.19–1.2.22, 1.4.10–1.4.12). Metformin and glyburide doses are from the FDA label as reused from the repository's earlier topic; insulin doses and the labour infusion regimen are the MOH figures (pp. 167, 170). Metformin crosses the placenta; discuss this with the woman. SFDA registration was not verified. Check hospital formulary.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: NICE: fasting 5.3, 1 hour after meals 7.8 or 2 hours 6.4 mmol/L; MOH: before meals below 95, 1 hour below 140, 2 hours below 120 mg/dL; MOH also HbA1c below 7% (NG3 1.3.5; MOH pp. 167–168)
Fasting and 1-hour post-meal daily on diet, tablets or single-dose insulin; fasting, pre-meal, 1-hour post-meal and bedtime daily on multiple daily insulin (NG3 1.3.2–1.3.3)
Fasting below 7.0 mmol/L: diet and exercise trial; targets missed after 1–2 weeks: metformin; then insulin; fasting 7.0 or above: insulin at once (NG3 1.2.18–1.2.22)
NICE: no later than 40 weeks plus 6 days, earlier if complications; MOH: induction at 39 weeks with good control, as clinically indicated otherwise (NG3 1.4.4–1.4.5; MOH p. 168)
Hourly capillary glucose, keep 4–7 mmol/L; IV dextrose and insulin if outside range (NG3 1.4.10, 1.4.12)
Blood glucose at 2 to 4 hours; feed within 30 minutes and every 2–3 hours; pre-feed glucose at least 2.0 mmol/L (NG3 1.5.3, 1.5.9)

guidelineComparison.title: Saudi MOH Pocket Manual (2014) versus NICE NG3 for antenatal management

values: Before meals below 95; 1 hour below 140; 2 hours below 120 mg/dL; HbA1c below 7% (pp. 167–168)
Metformin, then insulin; insulin first at fasting 7.0 or above (1.2.19–1.2.22)
Antenatal testing from 32 weeks; growth scans at 28, 32 and 36 weeks (p. 168)
Growth and fluid every 4 weeks 28–36 weeks; no routine wellbeing tests before 38 weeks (1.3.34–1.3.35)
Induction at 39 weeks with good control (p. 168)
No later than 40 weeks plus 6 days; earlier for complications (1.4.4–1.4.5)
Check every 2 hours; insulin infusion above 120 mg/dL (p. 170)

guidelineComparison.note: The guidelines disagree on drug order, timing of birth and labour monitoring; follow the local protocol. Conversions: 95 mg/dL is about 5.3 mmol/L, 140 mg/dL about 7.8 mmol/L and 120 mg/dL about 6.7 mmol/L, so the MOH 2-hour target is looser than NICE's 6.4 mmol/L.

teaching.scope: Women with gestational diabetes after diagnosis: glucose monitoring and targets, escalation to metformin or insulin, fetal surveillance, timing and mode of birth, glucose control in labour and caesarean, and neonatal glucose checks. Checked against the Saudi MOH Pocket Manual in Obstetrics & Gynaecology (2014) and NICE NG3. Sections: MOH pp. 166–171; NG3 recommendations 1.2.9–1.2.23, 1.3.1–1.3.5, 1.3.33–1.3.40, 1.4.1–1.4.12 and 1.5.1–1.5.11.
learningObjectives: Monitor and escalate treatment by fasting glucose and response to 1–2 weeks of diet and exercise.
Plan the timing and mode of birth, labour glucose control and newborn glucose checks.
pitfalls: Mixing mg/dL and mmol/L targets from the two guidelines.
Using HbA1c to judge control in the second and third trimesters.
Delaying insulin when fasting glucose is 7.0 mmol/L or above.
Discharging the baby before 24 hours or before glucose is stable.
keyPoints: Joint clinic review within 1 week and every 1–2 weeks after.
Fasting 7.0 mmol/L or above: insulin at once.
Labour glucose 4–7 mmol/L hourly (NICE); MOH checks every 2 hours.
Baby glucose at 2–4 hours; feed within 30 minutes.

references.title: MOH Pocket Manual in Obstetrics & Gynaecology, Saudi Ministry of Health
references.edition: MOH Pocket Manual in Obstetrics & Gynaecology, 2014

references.title: NICE NG3: Diabetes in pregnancy: management from preconception to the postnatal period

patientEducation: Explain that good control lowers the risk of a large baby, birth trauma, induction or caesarean, neonatal hypoglycaemia and stillbirth (NG3 1.2.10).
Teach glucose checks, fast-acting glucose for hypoglycaemia, and to seek urgent advice if unwell or hyperglycaemic (NG3 1.2.11, 1.3.14, 1.3.22).
Explain the plan for timing and mode of birth and for feeding the baby soon after birth (NG3 1.4.1, 1.5.9).
lifestyleAndDiet: See a dietitian and follow the advised diet (NG3 1.2.16; MOH p. 167).
Walk about 30 minutes after a meal or exercise regularly (NG3 1.2.17; MOH p. 166).
Aim for normoglycaemia, no ketosis and adequate weight gain (MOH p. 167).
mdtReferrals: Joint diabetes and antenatal clinic every 1–2 weeks (NG3 1.3.37–1.3.38).
Anaesthetist in the third trimester for obesity or autonomic neuropathy (NG3 1.4.8).
Neonatal team available around the clock at the delivery hospital (NG3 1.5.1).
dischargeCriteria: Glucose-lowering treatment stopped after birth and glucose checked (NG3 1.6.3; MOH p. 171).
Baby at least 24 hours old with stable glucose and feeding (NG3 1.5.6).
Postnatal diabetes test booked (see the postnatal follow-up topic).
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Joint clinic contact every 1–2 weeks to birth, then postnatal glucose test before community transfer and later diabetes testing (NG3 1.3.38, 1.6.8, 1.6.11; MOH p. 171).
